voice: A blustering, patronizing antagonist with a deliberately theatrical Irish-American persona, readable spelling, and pointed period sexism.

entries.text: Well now, Detective Ryan O'Riley, at your service. What might you be wanting, lass?
A reporter? Don't make me laugh. You're a girl. The Tribune hires men.
I thought that Crodfeather fellow was writing the robbery story.
It's a technical report, lass. I doubt you'd make much sense of it.
Persistent little thing, aren't you? Very well. Have a look.
Proper police work takes time, and I'm a very busy man. I haven't had a chance to follow up on one little burglary...
...A museum loses a knife--so what? People are being murdered left and right. Cars are being stolen. Booze is being smuggled into speakeasies...
...Pedestrians are being mugged, firebugs are setting half the city ablaze, the corner market is running out of grapes, and I've got a splitting headache!
...And who gets every crime in this district? Me! So I don't need some nosy girl reporter barging into my office to tell me my work is vague!
If you have more questions, bother the desk sergeant. I've wasted enough time on you.
